security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation for building deterministic HyperFrames video compositions. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, HTML ids, grep examples, and harness terminology; real residual risks are CDN script loading and explicit npx-based validation and render commands.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned local dependency or an integrity-checked bundled asset when users need offline or reproducible rendering.

remediation.issue: Validation guidance uses npx hyperframes commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx commands, and prefer a project-pinned hyperframes CLI version when available.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects can fail when timing, media placement, or sub-composition wiring is inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a clear contract for creating deterministic HTML video compositions.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required HyperFrames root structure and data timing attributes.
Guides standalone and modular composition architecture choices.
Defines how tracks, clips, sub-compositions, variables, and media elements should be wired.
Describes deterministic rendering rules for seekable timelines and safe animation properties.
Provides validation steps for linting, inspection, snapshots, preview, and render approval.
Covers Tailwind v4 usage patterns for browser-runtime compositions.
limitations: Does not provide the HyperFrames CLI implementation or runtime itself.
Does not cover detailed GSAP, Lottie, or Three.js animation APIs beyond contract boundaries.
Requires users to supply project assets, timing goals, and visual direction.
External CLI commands and rendering steps still need user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Create a renderable video composition
use_cases.description: Generate a HyperFrames index.html with correctly sized roots, clip timing, and a paused timeline.
use_cases.target_user: Motion designers using AI coding tools

use_cases.title: Structure a modular scene project
use_cases.description: Split a multi-scene video into sub-compositions with matching host ids, templates, and timeline keys.

use_cases.title: Validate deterministic render behavior
use_cases.description: Check timing, media placement, Tailwind class usage, and render gates before preview or final export.

prompt_templates.title: Start a minimal composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one simple scene.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal HyperFrames composition for a 10 second 1920 by 1080 video. Include one clip, one paused timeline, and valid data attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan scene structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this storyboard and recommend whether the HyperFrames project should be monolithic or modular. Explain the composition files, clip timing, and track layout.

prompt_templates.title: Wire sub-compositions
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a multi-scene project with reusable scene files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this HyperFrames project into sub-compositions. Ensure every host data-composition-id matches the internal template id and timeline key.

prompt_templates.title: Audit before render
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this HyperFrames project against the core contract. Check deterministic rendering, media placement, Tailwind class safety, unique ids, and validation commands.

output_examples.input: Build a short product intro video from three scenes.
output_examples.output: A project plan that uses one root composition, three timed scene slots, a separate audio track, and validation steps before preview.

output_examples.input: My sub-composition renders blank in the final output.
output: Check that style, script, and markup are inside the template.
Verify that host id, internal data-composition-id, and timeline key match.
Move video or audio elements to direct root children.

output_examples.input: Use Tailwind in a HyperFrames composition.
output_examples.output: Guidance to use visible complete class tokens, stable dimensions, and explicit CSS instead of runtime-only dynamic class generation.

best_practices: Read the relevant reference file before changing composition HTML.
Keep one paused timeline per composition and register it synchronously at page load.
Run validation and preview steps before final render, with user approval for render commands.
anti_patterns: Do not place video or audio inside sub-composition templates.
Do not rely on clocks, unseeded randomness, network state, or infinite repeats during render.
Do not build render-critical Tailwind class names only at runtime.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build HyperFrames HTML video compositions that follow the required runtime contract.

faq.question: Can it create a full video project?
faq.answer: Yes, it can guide project structure and composition authoring when you provide the concept, assets, and timing needs.

faq.question: Does it run the HyperFrames renderer?
faq.answer: No. It documents validation and render commands, but command execution depends on your local environment and approval.

faq.question: Does it support Tailwind?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Tailwind v4 runtime constraints and safe class patterns for HyperFrames compositions.

faq.question: Can it debug blank media output?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights common causes, including media inside templates, duplicate ids, and incorrect composition wiring.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
